content: Tolnaftate is an over-the-counter antifungal medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of athlete’s foot (tinea pedis) and ringworm (tinea corporis). It is also used to provide relief from symptoms such as itching, burning, and cracking of the skin. Common adverse reactions include irritation. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications: Athlete’s foot (tinea pedis) Ringworm (tinea corporis) Symptomatic relief of itching, burning, and cracking Directions for Use: Wash the affected area and dry thoroughly before application. Apply a thin layer of the medication over the affected area twice daily, in the morning and at night. Supervise children during use. For athlete’s foot, pay special attention to the spaces between the toes. Wear well-fitting, ventilated shoes, and change shoes and socks at least once daily. Use daily for four weeks. If the condition persists beyond this period, consult a doctor. To prevent athlete’s foot, apply once or twice daily (morning and/or night). This product is not effective for fungal infections of the scalp or nails. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adult) There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported use of Tolnaftate in adults. Non-guideline-supported use includes onychomycosis caused by dermatophytes. Contraindications There is limited information regarding contraindications for Tolnaftate in the drug label. Warnings For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Consult a doctor if there is no improvement within four weeks. Do not use in children under two years of age unless directed by a doctor. If swallowed, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately (1-800-222-1222). Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Irritation is a common adverse reaction.
